canonical_question: How does the stress value of 5.5 GPa at 300 K compare to the 6.2 GPa peak at 77 K in terms of the specific dislocation mobility?

question_variants.question: How does the stress value of 5.5 GPa at 300 K compare to the 6.2 GPa peak at 77 K in terms of the specific dislocation mobility?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence provides stress values for 300 K (5.5 GPa) and mentions 6.2 GPa at 77 K, but does not explicitly compare them in terms of specific dislocation mobility.

answers.answer: The text provides the 300 K stress value (5.5 GPa) but does not provide a specific comparison to 77 K (6.2 GPa) regarding dislocation mobility.
answers.measurement_outcome: At 300 K, stress in CoNiCrFeMn HEA NW reaches up to 5.5 GPa at around 5% strain
answers.boundary_limitation: No direct comparison of mobility provided
evidence_spans: Otto et al. [ [18] ] reported an increment in the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and elongation to fracture with decreasing temperature especially in the cryogenic range.
The tensile strength increased from 730 to 1280 MPa as temperature is lowered from ambient temperature (293 K) to cryogenic temperature (77 K).
At 77 K, onset of necking was delayed due to deformation induced nanotwinning with a high degree of work hardening resulting in increased ductility.
